Priya (support): FYI escalation from AcmeCorp — they reported a sudden p95/p99 tail spike on the hosted /v1/generate route for model-redwood-34b-quant. Started ~1987654200, p95 up from ~120ms to 600ms, p99 to ~1.2s, occasional 502s. Customer says loads are steady (no big spike). They attached traces showing GPU memory climb and a few OOM kills. @Jonah can you pick this up?

Jonah (eng-runtime): Looking. I pulled the stack traces and the per-GPU memory graph for the pool handling that model. Observations: GPU resident memory slowly increases during long chat sessions, KV cache size grows per-request (chat state). When it hits ~95% we see allocation stalls then retries -> token generation stalls -> tail latency. Also saw a kubelet OOMKilled event for one replica around 1987654258.

Jonah (eng-runtime): Pasted relevant excerpt from node logs:
```
[1987654258] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 3421 (llm-worker) score 1200 or sacrifice child
[1987654258] kernel: Killed process 3421 (llm-worker) total-vm:3123456kB, anon-rss:2890000kB, file-rss:0kB
```

Maria (eng-sre): That pattern matches fragmentation and KV growth. If chat sessions keep appending keys to a per-session cache without TTL, you get logical growth even if average request size is constant. jemalloc stats on the pod show high retained vs active ratio. Example:
```
allocated: 2.8G active: 2.6G metadata: 120M mapped: 4.1G retained: 1.5G
fragmentation: retained - active = 1.5G - 2.6G = -1.1G (=> high retention/mapping)
```
Not exact numbers but similar shape.

Alex (infra): We can try two immediate things: 1) force rolling restart of the pool (flushes KV + frees GPU allocations) and 2) temporarily route heavy chat users to the smaller quantized model variant (34b-int8) until we stabilize. Also we should throttle the largest batches coming from that route.

Tara (oncall): I'll run restart on 3 replicas in the pool now (staggered 30s). Patching in progress. Notifying customer that we are doing a rolling restart and routing changes as a temporary mitigation.

SRE-Bot: Deploy rollout started: pool/model-redwood-34b-quant -> rolling restart 3/8 replicas. Watch CPU/GPU and pod restarts.

Jonah (eng-runtime): After restart we saw immediate drop in p95 to ~140ms and p99 to ~210ms for ~10 minutes, then p99 climbed again as a few long-lived sessions re-accumulated KV state. So restart helps short-term but root cause is uncontrolled KV retention + allocator fragmentation.

Priya (support): Customer confirmed improved tail for ~20 minutes then slowdowns returned. They have long chat sessions (avg tokens ~12k/session), so this explains steady growth. Asking for timeline and permanent fix.

Maria (eng-sre): Short-term mitigations that helped in our test:
- Enforce per-session KV TTL (default 10m) and soft eviction when entries > N.
- Limit max_concurrent_batch_size per-worker to reduce peak working set (example: set MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=2048).
- Route active long-session customers to quantized variants automatically via routing policy.
- Add jemalloc env tweaks: `MALLOC_CONF=background_thread:true,dirty_decay_ms:1000,muzzy_decay_ms:1000` to encourage faster reuse of pages.

Jonah (eng-runtime): Config snippets we applied in the canary:
```yaml
env:
  - name: KV_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS
    value: "600"
  - name: KV_SOFT_LIMIT_ENTRIES
    value: "500000"
  - name: MAX_BATCH_TOKENS
    value: "2048"
  - name: MALLOC_CONF
    value: "background_thread:true,dirty_decay_ms:1000,muzzy_decay_ms:1000"
```
Also adjusted router policy to fallback to model-redwood-34b-int8 when session tokens > 8k.

Tara (oncall): After applying those, p95/p99 stayed in acceptable bounds for 30m. We're keeping the routing fallback for now. Customer notified.

Priya (support): They asked for repro steps so they can validate from their side — shared a minimal load script with them. Repro steps we gave:
1) Create a long chat session with repeated append operations until ~10k tokens.
2) Run a sustained request pattern: `wrk -t8 -c100 -d120s -s post.lua --latency http://api.redwood/v1/generate` where post.lua hits the same session id and sends ~300-500 token prompts each request.
3) Observe GPU resident set and `/metrics` kv_cache_entries per-worker.

Example wrk POST snippet (post.lua) we provided:
```lua
wrk.method = "POST"
wrk.headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
function request()
  body = JSON.encode({session_id = "test-session-001", prompt = "hello world"})
  return wrk.format(nil, "/v1/generate", nil, body)
end
```

Alex (infra): Long-term plans:
- Add per-route KV quotas and automatic soft-eviction when a session grows beyond thresholds.
- Implement periodic KV compaction/gc for inactive sessions.
- Improve allocator integration: explore switching to tcmalloc for workers that allocate lots of small objects or enabling jemalloc purging more aggressively.
- Add a telemetry alert that tracks retained vs active memory ratio and fires before OOM (e.g., retained/active > 1.2).

Jonah (eng-runtime): Follow-up items assigned:
- (Jonah) Add per-route TTL + soft eviction (ETA 2d).
- (Maria) Add jemalloc retained/active alert (ETA 1d).
- (Alex) Prototype routing policy for large-session fallback (ETA 3d).
- (Tara) Run broader fleet sweep for similar pools and apply MALLOC_CONF change canary (ETA today).

Priya (support): Customer is ok with those timelines, asked for a short doc with steps we took and remaining plan. I'll send a postmortem once fixes are deployed.

SRE-Bot: Incident summary draft created: incident/1987654321-memory-pressure -> severity: P2 -> retained.

Tara (oncall): Marking thread resolved for immediate action. Will monitor next 48h and update. If p99 creeps >500ms again we escalate to P1.

Jonah (eng-runtime): Notes for follow-up postmortem: collect heap/proc maps, jemalloc stats, kv_entry histograms, per-request kv growth traces, and customer session ids for repro. We should also check if quantization variants show less fragmentation and update recommended routing policies.

Priya (support): Thanks all — closing loop with customer now.

SupportBot: Ticket #ACME-5421 updated: mitigation applied, follow-up scheduled.

Maria (eng-sre): Adding final note — short restarts are cheap but don't fix root cause. Prioritize eviction + TTL + allocator tuning as permanent fixes.

Tara (oncall): I'll add a check in the runbook for this scenario (long-session KV growth -> memory pressure -> restart fallback).
